title: Six signs the operation is not keeping up with the business
author: Brad Berlin
description: Growth can hide operating problems for a while. Six signs a business has outgrown how its work is designed, and a first step that costs nothing.

title: Getting out of the day-to-day: an operator's approach
author: Brad Berlin
description: Owners stay trapped in daily operations because of design, not discipline. A five-step redesign of decision rights, ownership, and cadence.

title: Own the Workflow Before You Add Another Subscription
author: Brad Berlin
description: When software subscriptions help, when they create more work, and why the workflow should be clear before another tool is added.

title: What I Actually Look At in a Construction Operations Audit
author: Brad Berlin
description: An operations audit is not a software pitch. It is watching where the friction in a construction business actually lives. Here is what I look at, and why.

title: You Have Ten Years of Bid History. Most of It You Cannot Use.
author: Brad Berlin
description: The best estimating data a commercial GC owns is its own past bids, but it is trapped in scattered files. How historical bid data becomes a cost database you can use.

title: You Bought Togal and Building Connected. The Gap Between Them Is Still Manual.
author: Brad Berlin
description: You bought good takeoff and bid software. Estimating still feels slow because the friction lives in the hand-offs between the tools, where your estimator stands.

title: Hire Another Estimator, or Make the Four You Have Faster?
author: Brad Berlin
description: The instinct is to reach for a fifth estimator. Before hiring, check whether the real constraint is estimating capacity or workflow coordination.

title: Where the Hours Actually Go in a Commercial Construction Bid
author: Brad Berlin
description: Estimators assume bid prep time lives in the takeoff. After sitting with estimating teams, here is where the hours in a commercial construction bid actually go.
